body: [A10] Clue from [R370-3](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/pull/604#issuecomment-5860812832) (PR #604): in all three non-stops (talker cycles 13, 24 and 75), the DUT sent its own MRP LeaveAll within 0.1 s of the bridge's Listener `Lv`. The stopping cycles 1-5 show no such coincidence. A LeaveAll timer firing inside the withdrawal window, and re-asserting state that keeps the stream running, is the first hypothesis to test. The records are published at `review-evidence/75-r1/author-r3/talker-013,024,075/msrp.tsv`.

[A10] **Analysis done; the fix is in the processor.** A deterministic SRP-engine simulation reproduces the mechanism. The engine ages its Listener registrar (IN to LV) at LeaveAll timer expiry, before its own LeaveAll is transmitted. A Listener Leave arriving in that window finds LV, does not unregister, and the stream stays active (`hdl/srp/KL_srp_top.sv:1125`, `KL_srp_talker_fsm.sv:564,630,693,698` in the processor). All three bench non-stops, and none of the 97 stops, match that timing. **Donor issue:** Mister-M-alt/protocol-processor-control-plane-avb-milan#127 moves the registrar event to the transmit action. The parent then adopts the pin with a CRF STREAM_STOP regression. **Decision:** LV + rLv semantics stay as documented. A stop target stricter than the table for a genuine LeaveAll cycle would need its own requirement decision, so this issue's acceptance 3 is read as "within one PDU period of a withdrawal that reaches an IN registrar".

[A10] The processor side of the LeaveAll fix is merged: processor PR #130, merge `97bd3786`, closing processor issue #127. This issue stays open for the parent pin-adoption lane. That lane adopts the new processor pin with the CRF STREAM_STOP regression, together with the #606 processor fix once processor PR #129 merges.

[A10] The processor fix for this issue is merged (processor PR #130, `97bd3786`). The parent pin adoption and the committed CRF STREAM_STOP regression run in the combined lane assigned on #606. The bench re-measure (item 3) follows on the next image.

[A10] Two facts from the #75 bench record ([R371-3](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/pull/604) S10) that bear on this issue. Both come from the three non-stop holds (cycles 13, 24 and 75):
- **No bridge LeaveAll** crossed the tap between the disconnect and reconnect responses. So a lost or ignored single `Lv` had no MRP recovery event before reconnect.
- **The first Listener re-declaration** came at least 2.0024 s after the withdrawal: 2.0173 s in cycle 24 and 2.0734 s in cycle 13. That rules out a race with a quick re-declaration for these cycles.

Source: the #75 findings page, lines 611-671 at merge `1fa2357f`.

[A10] Ruling on the reading of #608 item 3 ("stop within one PDU of the withdrawal"), after lane B2 ([A440], REVIEW READY 5885779526) on the dev `13eda870` image.

**The bar is a withdrawal that reaches an IN registrar.** 802.1Q-2014 Table 10-4: rLv! moves an IN registrar to LV and starts its leave timer. In LV, a further rLv! changes nothing. The registration ends, and the talker's licence closes, when the leave timer expires.

In cycle 22, the DUT's own LeaveAll crossed the tap 1.390 ms before the bridge's `Lv`. That LeaveAll had already moved the registrar to LV, so the bridge's `Lv` met an LV registrar. Streaming on through the 2 s hold, which is shorter than LeaveTime, is the standard's behaviour, not a talker defect.

- **#608 item 3 on this image:** PASS, 99 of 99 withdrawals that reached an IN registrar stopped within one PDU. STREAM_STOP counted each stop. There was one LV case, down from 3 non-stop holds of 100 on `9e9954e9`.
- **The LV case itself:** the talker stops at leave-timer expiry. That still needs grading. I am filing it for the processor program: a simulation arm in which a withdrawal meets an LV registrar after a LeaveAll, with the stop asserted at the leave-timer expiry.
- **#75 on this image:** 99 of 99 demonstrated restarts within 1 s (maximum 0.139 s), with no growth across cycles. Cycle 22 had no restart to measure, because the stream never stopped. No additional cycle is required.

[A10] Correction to my ruling [5885808887](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/608#issuecomment-5885808887), after [R404-1](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/pull/622#issuecomment-5886414299) F3.

The rLv!-in-LV step (802.1Q-2014 Table 10-4) is still standard behaviour. But the LV state in cycle 22 came from a DUT-side deviation:
- the bridge's MSRP LeaveAll crossed the tap 0.401 s before the DUT's own LeaveAll;
- a conformant participant restarts its leavealltimer on a received LeaveAll and sends none of its own (Table 10-5 rLA!, clause 10.6);
- the processor at `c951a9ff` does not, as recorded in processor issue #108;
- across lane B2's session, 67 of 112 captures show a DUT LeaveAll less than 10 s after a received bridge LeaveAll.

**Corrected reading:**
- **#608 item 3 on this image:** 99 of 99 withdrawals that reached an IN registrar stopped within one PDU.
- **The cycle-22 non-stop** is attributed to the processor #108 deviation, not accepted as standard behaviour. Processor PR #133 (lane C1, in review) implements the rLA! restart, which removes this class of LV window.
- **After the pin-adoption lane carries #133,** the bench re-runs the 100-cycle withdrawal. Only then is #608 item 3 met without qualification.
- **Processor #134** (grading the LV-registrar stop) still stands, because an LV window can also come from a peer.
